ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, founders, and authorized signatories against the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, the Egyptian Terrorist Entities and Terrorists Registration Committee list (established by Law No. 8 of 2015), OFAC (SDN) lists, and the domestic EMLCU watchlist, in accordance with Law No. 80/2002 and its Executive Regulations. Enhanced due diligence is required for politically exposed persons (PEPs), including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification, and such information must be kept on file for at least five years after the business relationship ends. The corporate records must contain a current UBO declaration signed by the legal representative with liability for falsification under the Egyptian Penal Code.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI Portal – Company Name Reservation (https://www.gafi.gov.eg) and the Commercial Registry of the Ministry of Trade and Industry (for duplicate domain registration check) via the online incorporation module of GAFI.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_document: Arabic is the official language. The proposed company name must be in Arabic script, or in Latin script accompanied by a mandatory Arabic transliteration accepted by the Commercial Registry. The legal form shall be indicated in the name as 'LLC' (English) or 'ذ.م.م' (Arabic abbreviation for a limited liability company). For foreign-investment companies, the name may include a foreign-derived trade name, but the Arabic transliteration shall be in standard Egyptian transliteration rules to avoid phonetic confusion. The name shall not conflict with any existing registered trademark or company name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: An applicant may submit an administrative appeal to the head of GAFI’s Name Approval Committee within 15 days from the date of rejection. The appeal must include the original rejection notice, a statement of legal grounds, and a revised name proposal. GAFI shall issue a written decision within 15 working days. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may initiate annulment proceedings before the Administrative Court within 60 days of receipt of the denial. Name reservations may be extended once for an additional 30 days upon payment of a renewal fee, provided that the original reservation has not been assigned to a third party. If no extension is received, the reservation lapses automatically.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible only as a supplementary commercial address, but not as the statutory registered office for this industrial manufacturing entity. The Investor must maintain a physical registered and administrative office in Egypt, which is deemed the legal place of service of notices and the seat of the company for jurisdictional purposes. GAFI and the Egyptian Commercial Registry will not approve a virtual office as a substitute for the mandatory physical address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-to-high estimated probability: 40% risk of an unannounced on‑site inspection by GAFI or the Industrial Development Authority (IDA) within the first 12 months after incorporation, and a further 30% risk in the second fiscal year, to verify commercial substance and conformity with the filed registered address and investment incentives. These inspections are ordinarily unannounced and may include verification of installed machinery, workforce presence, and physical infrastructure.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 as amended by Law No. 4 of 2009 (Limited Liability Company provisions, Articles 94-134) read with the Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and its Executive Regulations; Commercial Registry Law No. 34 of 1976; Industrial Licensing Law No. 15 of 2017 and implementing Prime Ministerial Decrees; fundamental corporate filings administered electronically via GAFI e-SARMED platform.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) — One-Stop Shop and Companies Establishment Department, Cairo; subsequent registration at the competent Commercial Registry Office (السجل التجاري) under the Ministry of Justice.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Contract and Arabic Articles of Association (Memorandum of Association) registered with GAFI plus application for issuance of the Certificate of Establishment (شهادة تأسيس الشركة).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: LLC minimum issued capital is EGP 50,000; at least 25% of subscribed capital must be paid in cash upon incorporation into a blocked temporary escrow account maintained at a licensed Egyptian bank (Company proposed capital EGP 600,000; initial deposit 25% = EGP 150,000); the residual 75% must be fully paid within five (5) years; foreign currency subscriptions may be admitted at the prevailing Central Bank of Egypt exchange rate with inward remittance evidence.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD OF MANAGERS RESOLUTION OF [LLC NAME] — adopted in Cairo: 1. RESOLVED, that the issued share capital of EGP 600,000 (1,000 quotas) be fully subscribed by the Founders; 25% (EGP 150,000) shall be paid into a blocked escrow account before registration. 2. RESOLVED, that the registered office per Article 5 of the Articles of Association, at [address], Cairo, be adopted. 3. RESOLVED, that [Name], [Name] and [Name] be appointed Managers with joint authority, and [CPA Firm] be appointed auditor. 4. RESOLVED, that the Managers are authorized to complete commercial and tax registration, industrial and environmental licensing, and bank account opening.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Legal Form Eligibility Check and Company Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) — e-SARMED Electronic Incorporation Portal, Cairo One-Stop Shop
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the GAFI e-SARMED portal and confirm LLC eligibility for manufacturing scope ISIC v4 code 2930; submit three alternative Arabic company names with Latin transliteration, each indicating limited liability nature; obtain the name reservation certificate (حجز اسم) valid for 60 days; obtain preliminary 'No Legal Obstacle' review from the GAFI Legal Desk for the objects clause covering manufacture of High-Power DC Ultra-Fast Electric Vehicle Chargers.
required_dossiers: Notarized copies of founders' national IDs or passports with Arabic translation where applicable
Proposed Arabic company name and three alternative names
Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association in Arabic
Statement of object clause referencing ISIC v4 code 2930 and EV charger manufacturing
KYC forms and source-of-funds declarations for founders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name or objects clause is queried, submit corrective alternatives within 15 days without a fresh fee; a reasoned GAFI refusal may be challenged before the GAFI Board of Directors within 30 days under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Articles of Association and Payment of 25% Capital into Escrow
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public Office (كاتب العدل / التوثيق) and a licensed Egyptian Bank for the blocked escrow account
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Each founder executes the final Arabic Articles of Association before the Notary Public; the Managers-elect open a temporary blocked escrow account in the name of the 'company under formation' at a licensed Egyptian bank and deposit not less than 25% of subscribed capital (EGP 150,000 of EGP 600,000); the bank issues a capital deposit certificate confirming the blockage until GAFI registration; non-resident founders must deposit in convertible currency and obtain an inward remittance certificate.
required_dossiers: GAFI name reservation receipt
Executed Articles of Association signed by all shareholders
Cash deposit slip or SWIFT credit advice for the escrow account
Bank capital blockage certificate (شهادة قيد بالمحفظة)
Power of attorney for non-resident signatories, notarized and legalized or apostilled
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries beneficial ownership, supplement with the ultimate beneficial owner statement and source-of-funds evidence; if the Notary flags a defective subscription clause, re-execute the Articles with corrected capitalization before registration without penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GAFI Incorporation Filing and Issuance of the Certificate of Establishment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Companies Establishment and Registration Department (One-Stop Shop)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the notarized Articles of Association, bank capital deposit certificate, and name reservation number to the e-SARMED platform; pay the assessed GAFI incorporation fees and stamp duty; GAFI verifies legal compliance and issues the Certificate of Establishment (شهادة تأسيس الشركة) with a preliminary commercial registration and tax prefix, automatically forwarding the file to the Commercial Registry and Tax Authority.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Association originals
Bank capital blockage certificate
Name reservation certificate
Payment order and receipts for incorporation fees and stamp duty
Lease or landlord consent for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to the final query letter within 15 working days with corrected documents; if the certificate is withheld over capital remittance, submit a supplementary bank confirmation; appeal to the GAFI Investment Window committees under Law No. 72 of 2017 upon rejection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registry Registration and Tax Card / VAT Number
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Competent Commercial Registration Office (السجل التجاري المختص); Egyptian Tax Authority (مصلحة الضرائب المصرية)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the GAFI certificate with the competent Commercial Registry within 15 days from the establishment date; pay registry fees and obtain the commercial register record and extract; thereafter apply for the unified electronic tax card (رقم ضريبي) and, where annual taxable turnover exceeds EGP 500,000, compulsory VAT registration under the VAT Law No. 67 of 2016; order the company seal and statutory books.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Establishment issued by GAFI
Commercial registration application form (نموذج 1) with manager authorizations
Notarized lease of premises and address certificate
Founders' IDs and specimen signatures of the Managers
Tax Authority registration form with authorized signatory passport
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late registration may be cured by voluntary payment of a nominal monthly late fine (capped at approximately EGP 300 per month); if the file is returned because the factory address differs from the objects clause, execute a notarial amending resolution before re-filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial License Application under Law 15 of 2017 and IDA Facility Authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Industrial Development Authority (IDA) — Industrial Licensing Directorate, automatic / instant-track category for light electronic assembly
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the industrial authorization application electronically through IDA for the EV charger assembly line (light manufacturing, soldering and testing); attach the factory lease or title deed, zoning permit, process flow and machinery list; the application is processed under the 'silence is approval' rule, with a license deemed granted after thirty (30) business days of authority inaction; pay the licensing fee and receive the Industrial Operation License (رخصة تشغيل المنشأة الصناعية), renewable every five years and preconditioned for factory energy supply and investment incentives.
required_dossiers: GAFI establishment certificate and commercial register extract
Lease or ownership deed of the factory building with zoning and land-use certificate
Process flow diagram and machinery list
Stamp-duty paid IDA application forms
Civil Defense preliminary approval and fire safety drawings
EEAA environmental reply or pending filing receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If IDA requests corrective data, file a variation of facility plan within 30 days; after 30 days of silence, issue a registered-mail deemed-approval notice; any formal rejection may be appealed to the IDA Grievance Committee within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Environmental Compliance (EEAA) and Civil Defense Final Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) — Environmental Licensing Directorate; Civil Defense Department of the Ministry of Interior
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Category B Simplified Environmental Impact Assessment Form and Environmental Management Plan with EEAA and obtain the Environmental Compliance Certificate (شهادة القيد البيئي) before production start; separately obtain the final Civil Defense fire-safety clearance for the plant, including fire suppression, means of egress, and structural load inspection; the Civil Defense certificate is attached to the factory inspection file and renewed annually.
required_dossiers: EEAA Form B and Environmental Management Plan with wastewater and emissions data
Layout of soldering area with VOC extraction and e-waste storage zone
Civil Defense application with structural load certificate
Hazardous waste handling contract with an EEAA-licensed carrier
Approved fire alarm and fire suppression plans
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: EEAA screening returns within 30 days; if the project is upgraded to Category C requiring a full EIA public consultation, appoint a licensed environmental consultant and resubmit; an environmental rejection may be appealed to the Environmental Complaint Committee within 30 days while implementing the stated corrective operational measures.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Industrial Development Authority (IDA) — الهيئة العامة للتنمية الصناعية, Industrial Licensing Directorate, Cairo Investor Service Center
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Industrial Facility Operating License (رخصة تشغيل المنشأة الصناعية) — automatic-approval license category for light electronic assembly granted under Law No. 15 of 2017, valid for five (5) years and renewable

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) — جهاز شئون البيئة, Ministry of Environment, operating under Law No. 4 of 1994 as amended by Law No. 9 of 2009
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B (simplified EIA screening): submission of Form B with a site-specific Environmental Management Plan; no full public EIA consultation required for light electronic assembly, but the Environmental Compliance Certificate (شهادة القيد البيئي) must be issued before production commencement
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge to public sewer per Decree 44 of 2000: pH 6.0-9.5, BOD5 ≤ 60 mg/L, COD ≤ 100 mg/L, TSS ≤ 50 mg/L, lead ≤ 1 mg/L, total heavy metals ≤ 5 mg/L; point-source air emissions per Decree 338 of 1995 under Law 4 of 1994, including particulate matter ≤ 50 mg/Nm³ and VOC capture or abatement efficiency ≥ 90% at soldering stations; hazardous electronic waste (solder dross, e-waste) must be segregated, labeled, and transferred only to EEAA-licensed carriers and treatment facilities under a hazardous waste manifest per the Executive Regulations of Law 4 of 1994

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Civil Defense Clearance (موافقة الحماية المدنية) under Civil Defense Law No. 3 of 1978: fire load and means-of-egress verification, structural load inspection certificate for plant floors and mezzanines, and approval of fire alarm and suppression layouts issued by the Civil Defense Department of the Ministry of Interior; the industrial license remains conditioned on this annual clearance and on workplace occupational safety compliance with Ministry of Manpower standards.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) - the national revenue authority of the Arab Republic of Egypt under the Ministry of Finance; official e-services portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg; e-invoicing and e-receipt platforms: https://einvoicing.eta.gov.eg and https://ereceipt.eta.gov.eg
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 - Incorporate the LLC through the GAFI one-stop-shop and obtain the Commercial Registration Certificate and incorporation extract. Step 2 - Apply for the Tax Card (national TIN) at the competent ETA district office or through the ETA e-portal using the unified tax registration application. Step 3 - Submit the statutory KYC documentation pack: certified Arabic Articles of Association, Commercial Registration Certificate, registered office lease or ownership proof, board and shareholder resolutions, valid passports or national IDs of all managers and shareholders, and a notarized power of attorney appointing the Egyptian tax representative. Step 4 - File the VAT registration application (ETA Form No. 1) when actual or expected taxable turnover exceeds the statutory threshold; registration must be completed within 30 days of passing the mandatory threshold. Step 5 - ETA issues the Tax Card and VAT registration certificate, typically within 2-4 weeks of complete documentation; thereafter the taxpayer must enroll in the e-invoicing API platform (obtain KID and PIN credentials), open an Egyptian foreign-currency bank account for export proceeds, and maintain statutory accounting records under the Egyptian commercial and tax laws.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - an Egyptian LLC is a resident corporate taxpayer under Law No. 91 of 2005, taxed at entity level on worldwide income at the standard 22.5% corporate rate; no pass-through eligibility exists; distributions are not deductible; the entity is subject to full CIT, salary tax, withholding tax, and VAT compliance; special territorial or tax-exempt treatment is not automatic and requires a qualifying investment license under Law No. 72 of 2017 or registration in an approved free zone / investment zone / SCZone regime.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egypt does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime and has no hybrid-mismatch entity election. The principal statutory elections available are: (1) optional VAT registration for annual taxable turnover between EGP 50,000 and EGP 500,000; (2) consolidated Egyptian corporate tax group filing for subsidiaries held directly or indirectly at least 95%; (3) recognition-pattern election for long-term construction contracts (percentage-of-completion vs completed-contract) as permitted by the Income Tax Law and its executive regulations; (4) selection of the general tax regime vs the incentivized investment/free-zone/SCZone regime under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 for eligible manufacturing entities; and (5) depreciation method elections within the ETA-prescribed fixed-asset depreciation schedules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT - Value Added Tax under Egyptian Law No. 67 of 2016 (as amended) and its Executive Regulations
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Mandatory VAT registration is triggered when the value of taxable supplies exceeds EGP 500,000 during the preceding 12 months; optional or voluntary registration is available when annual taxable turnover exceeds EGP 50,000; the registration application must be submitted to the ETA within 30 days after the mandatory threshold is crossed.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time e-invoicing under ETA Decision No. 646 of 2020, with e-receipt obligations for B2C retail sales. Registered taxpayers must use ETA-approved billing software integrated via ETA REST APIs, transmit every B2B invoice in the prescribed XML schema to the ETA e-invoicing platform for real-time validation and fiscal clearance before issuance to the buyer, and embed a unique ETA-issued UUID and QR code stamp on the final invoice PDF. Non-cleared, duplicate, or off-portal invoices are deemed invalid and trigger rejection, monetary fines, and ETA information-technology audits.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero rating at 0% VAT applies to goods physically exported outside Egypt and to certain services supplied to non-residents for use wholly outside Egypt. The exporter must hold a valid VAT registration certificate; goods must exit Egyptian customs territory under a valid export customs declaration with ownership and risk transferred to the non-resident buyer; consideration must be paid in convertible foreign currency and repatriated through an Egyptian licensed bank; and the exporter must retain the full statutory file comprising customs, transport, contract, and inward remittance evidence. Input VAT attributable to exported goods and related overheads is reclaimable through monthly periodical returns via offset against output VAT or by direct cash refund after ETA verification.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (export SAD / customs export entry) stamped by the Egyptian Customs Authority - mandatory
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical exportation and destination - mandatory
Inward Remittance Certificate / foreign-currency credit advice issued by an Egyptian bank evidencing receipt of export proceeds - mandatory
Commercial export invoice and underlying sales contract or purchase order - supporting
Certificate of Origin where required by the destination market or financing bank - supporting
Input VAT tax invoices and supporting overhead documents matching the exported goods for the refund claim - supporting
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ETA performs desk reviews, field audits, and cross-verification of customs, bank, and e-invoicing data on every zero-rated export and VAT refund claim. Missing, inconsistent, or fraudulent documentation reverses the 0% rate to the standard 14% VAT on the full export value, denies the input VAT offset or refund, and opens the file to retrospective reassessment for up to 5 years (extended in fraud cases). Financial sanctions include monthly late-payment surcharges on the reassessed VAT, statutory civil fines of EGP 10,000-50,000 under Law No. 67 of 2016 for false declarations and documentation, removal from the authorized e-invoicing and export facilitation regimes, and criminal liability including imprisonment for fraudulent refund claims or forgery of export documentation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) — Banking Law No. 194 of 2020, Foreign Exchange Regulatory Department; co-regulatory oversight by the Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) for non-bank financial instruments and the General Authority for Investment (GAFI) for capital entry/exit recording.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt maintains a unified managed-float exchange rate regime (post-March 2024), yielding de jure and de facto convertibility on the current account (trade in goods/services, royalties, dividends to non-residents) with minimal documentary hurdles. The capital account remains segmented: full convertibility for portfolio inflows and FDI under GAFI registration, repatriation permitted upon bank confirmation of certified underlying transactions (audited financials, tax clearance), and residual administrative scrutiny for outbound payments with a value exceeding USD 100,000 per transaction. Profit remittances are lawful via banks using the 'Form 15 (Dividend Repatriation)' mechanism plus CBE-prescribed code 'D/L' declarations, but banks may impose operational delays during episodic USD liquidity constraints. Egypt imposes no general capital controls tax, yet all FX transactions must be routed through CBE-licensed banks; inter-company loans require CBE approval when tenor < 2 years or when creditor-in-substance is a related offshore entity.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: CBE Circular (Implementation Rules of the Central Bank and Banking System Law) mandates full repatriation (no mandated surrender/conversion percentage) of export proceeds into an Egyptian bank account within 90 days from the bill of lading date (CBE Regulation No. 759/2017 as amended; CBE circular of Dec 2022 suspended forced conversion). However, per CBE Directive of March 2024 (eliminating the 100% surrender ratio), exporters retain full discretion to keep USD/foreign currency balances in Export Proceeds Accounts for up to 120 days, without default obligation to sell to the CBE. Failure to repatriate within the statutory timeline triggers bank-initiated CBE reporting, potential port/import blacklisting, and forfeiture of FX-dealing privileges; the LLC must file a detailed 'Export Proceeds Repatriation Statement (Form-Export/01)' quarterly for any shipment above USD 50,000.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: LOW — Egyptian law (CBE Law No. 194/2020, Article 221 under banking exclusivity) prohibits offshore digital EMIs (Wise, Revolut, Airwallex, Payoneer) from directly opening Egyptian corporate accounts or providing domestic payment services without a CBE payment-facilitator license and an Egyptian physical presence; local fintech licensing (e.g., via CBE's Regulatory Sandbox) exists but does not cover multi-jurisdictional treasury clearing. Offshore EMI accounts may be used purely as auxiliary receivables collectors for non-Egyptian buyers, but transferring proceeds into Egypt triggers full repatriation rules; compliance risk is HIGH if the LLC relies on such rails as its principal settlement channel. Recommended architecture: local CBE-licensed bank as the treasury spine; offshore EMI usage strictly limited to EU/UK collection with daily sweeps to the Egyptian operational account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Egyptian CBE KYC Rules (Decree No. 115/2021) mandate physical presence for corporate account opening: the board of directors (or two authorized joint signatories holding Egyptian-National-ID or institutional passport) MUST appear at the branch for a face-to-face interview; remote video KYC is not permitted for corporates. In addition, the Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) — any natural person >25% ownership — must appear physically (or at a notarized Egyptian embassy/consulate interview abroad with apostilled POA). The General Manager and Financial Controller must each submit specimen signatures in wet-ink. There is no legal waiver for non-resident directors; a non-resident director may delegate via a notarized Power-of-Attorney valid in Egypt, but at least one Egyptian resident authorized signatory must be present for the bank interview and subsequent compliance reviews.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign UBO with >25% direct/indirect beneficial holding, especially residency in the UK/Mainland China/EU where source of wealth cannot be easily corroborated by Egyptian bank compliance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank-verified Certificate of Incumbency from the UAE/UK Registrar, bank-reference letter from a top-50 global bank (standard one-page source-of-wealth summary), audited financials of the parent (or of the ultimate natural person's investment portfolio) for the last 2 years, sworn declaration of source of funds, and a memorandum of corporate structure tracing every ownership tranche to a natural person.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Company name/beneficiary list matches SDN/OFSI ofac or UN Security Council Resolution 1267 sanctions databases (false positive due to Arabic-name transliteration or EV-industry sponsor in Iran-linked territory)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Exact-match letters from the General Authority for Investment (GAFI) Certificate of Incorporation, national ID and passport bio-pages, adverse-media screening report from a compliance-grade provider (Dow Jones/LexisNexis), a written legal opinion from Egyptian counsel confirming no sanctioned nexus, and an email/phone verification trail from CBE's Misr AML & Counterterrorism Unit (AML/CTF) confirming identity resolution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction profile mismatch — early-stage company seeking to wire large inbound equity > USD 1,000,000 within 90 days of signing, without a proven operational history in Egypt
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed board-resolution approving capital injection, GAFI-issued investment certificate and capital registration proof (Form A/C), 12-month cash-flow forecast for the DC-fast-charger manufacturing project, relevant government tender/import documentation evidencing committed procurement, and a compliance undertaking to operate solely pursuant to CBE 'Unified FX Declaration Form (Ex-002)' per transfer.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing: (a) SWIFT MT103 wire from parent to the Egyptian operational account with payment purpose code 'GAFI-C01 (Equity Capital Contribution)' and reference to the serialized GAFI Investment Certificate; (b) entry via CBE's single secured ledger; (c) confirmation within 3-5 business days through the 'Egyptian FX Capital Entry System (FX-E)' after submission of Form (Capital/)GAFI-1 and the notarized capital deposit certificate from the receiving bank; (d) the LLC must separately file a 'Capital Entry Verification' with CBE and corresponding GAFI shares-issue registration, converting the inflow to issued share capital (minimum not required, but statutory requirement to register actual subscribed amount with GAFI). Prohibition: equity injection may NOT be received through an offshore account or a money-service business intermediary; the sole legal route is a direct wire to a CBE-licensed bank account held in the LLC's name.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Standard clearing rails: (a) SWIFT MT103 for non-LC operational payments (freight, spare-part imports, partially paid services, salaries above EGP threshold) routed through the corporate bank's direct custody and CBE-reportable F-Form; (b) SWIFT MT700 (Commercial Letter of Credit) for high-value component shipments from China/Germany — irrevocable, confirmed or unconfirmed by the Egyptian bank, with UCP600 governing, terms typically 60-120 days usance, payable against a full set of clean-on-board bills of lading, commercial invoice, packing list, and certificate-of-origin; (c) SWIFT MT202/COV for correspondent-bank interbank settlement during cross-BDC transfers; (d) Egypt-QIZ/GAFTA expedited payment rail for inputs sourced under qualified industrial zone rules. All outbound FX disbursements require: the CBE Unified Declaration Form (UD-1), underlying commercial contract, tax certificate confirming withholding tax on services, and, for USD > 10,000 per individual shipment, a bank discretion under 'import verification' requiring 6-month track record of PFI (Proforma Invoice) and customs release proof.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable EGP/USD FX Forwards (CBE-registered, tenor up to 180 days, available only against genuine trade transactions with documentary evidence; CBE Law 194/2020 permissions incorporated into authorized bank Treasury Standard, as reaffirmed by the March-2024 unpeg directive)

Offshore Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDF) on EGP, permitted for Egyptian corporates only via international broker/legally equivalent contract with a licensed global bank (e.g., LSE-China bilateral deal); settlement reference to CBE-published central or interbank rate; no physical delivery in EGP; effective after the 2024 free-floating alignment

Cross-Currency Swaps (CCS) between EGP and USD/EUR/CNY — permissible for long-tenor capital expenditure hedging of the EV-charger infrastructure, conducted onshore with a licensed Egyptian bank needing to demonstrate underlying public-project or capital commitment (rate-swap legs net-settled quarterly)
Offshore-linked synthetic options (call/put spreads) subject to bank's internal collateral requirements; outright options are generally unavailable on EGP domestically

Commodity-price downside hedges via handled exchange-traded futures (nickel/copper/aluminum) through international broker accounts (separate from CBE approval) — not classified as FX instruments but embedded in the treasury policy for raw-material cost protection

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Registration Annual Renewal (Annual Registry Fee) - LLC
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the anniversary date of the company's commercial registration; registry fee is payable annually with the renewal statement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment surcharges under Commercial Registry Rules; 12-month continuous non-renewal triggers administrative strike-off of the legal entity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting and Filing of Audited Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ordinary General Assembly must convene within 6 months of fiscal year-end; certified financial statements must be filed with GAFI within 30 days after approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines under Companies Law No. 159/1981, suspension of corporate license or certificates, and non-issuance of governmental clearance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Form No. 8)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after the end of the tax year; ETA may grant one additional month upon application
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fixed late-filing fine in EGP plus monthly delay interest on unpaid tax; chronic non-filing triggers enforceable collection, criminal referral, and asset seizure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Payroll and Withholding Tax Annual Reconciliation (WHT Annual Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed within 4 months after the close of the tax year, aligned with the annual corporate tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty up to 100% of evaded WHT plus monthly delay interest; repeated violations expose directors to criminal liability under Income Tax Law No. 91/2005.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: All Egyptian limited liability companies are required to appoint at least one certified public auditor; no size-based audit exemption applies under the Companies Law.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), substantially aligned with IFRS, are mandatory for statutory annual financial statements; regulated entities apply IFRS as endorsed by local regulators.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Companies must maintain a current register of beneficial owners and file ownership or UBO updates with the Commercial Registry whenever share transfers occur; UBO data is confirmed annually at commercial registration renewal and disclosed to auditors for verification.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 120 - USD 350 per annum for registered office or corporate agent
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 600 - USD 2,000 per annum for statutory audit by a certified auditor

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Flat 10% tax on profits for qualifying Free Zone and Special Economic Zone projects, including the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZone); 50% deduction of total investment costs from taxable profits over 7 years for manufacturing projects (including ISIC 2930 EV charger production) under Investment Law No. 72/2017 as amended; additional State export subsidy programmes may reduce the effective rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Model No. 200 (Corporate Tax Return) submitted electronically via the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) e-Taxation platform (services.eta.gov.eg).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual corporate return; quarterly advance CIT instalments (Form 205) and monthly withholding tax returns are required separately.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 4 months after the fiscal year-end (calendar year-end filers must file and pay by 30 April of the following year).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: ETA-issued 9-digit TIN of the Egyptian LLC.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the Egyptian LLC TIN; no foreign parent TIN should be substituted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal form, commercial register number, tax card number, and Articles of Association details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose the foreign shareholder's country of incorporation and ownership percentage in the related-party annex.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Primary ISIC Code 2930 (manufacture of electric vehicle charging equipment).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm no deemed permanent establishment arises from mere export sales financed by letters of credit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total invoiced revenue from DC fast charger sales, net of discounts and returns.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Convert export proceeds at the Central Bank of Egypt official rate and retain LC and wire transfer documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: COGS comprising imported components, direct manufacturing labour, and production overheads.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Separately disclose import duties and freight charges and reconcile to customs declarations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Administrative, marketing, and financing expenses incurred for the Egyptian business.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany management fees and royalties are deductible only if arm's length and supported by an Egyptian TP file.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit adjusted for non-deductible provisions, depreciation differences, and transfer pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach Form 40 (TP Disclosure) if related-party transactions exceed the statutory thresholds.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income multiplied by 22.5%, less quarterly advance payments, foreign tax credits, and other credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If treaty-reduced dividend WHT is applied, attach the approved Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial ownership declaration.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: administrative fine of EGP 5,000 to EGP 50,000. Late payment: 2% monthly surcharge on unpaid tax, capped at 100% of the tax due. Non-filing or false filing triggers automatic ETA assessment, bank account blocking, and potential criminal tax evasion prosecution.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% final withholding tax on dividend distributions to all shareholders, including non-resident shareholders (Article 56 of Law No. 91 of 2005).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Egyptian paying entity must file the ETA treaty relief application with the International Taxation Department before the distribution order, attaching the recipient's valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC), a beneficial ownership declaration, and a detailed DTA position paper. Approved treaty rates apply at source; refund claims must be made within 5 years and require proof of Egyptian withholding. The EV charger manufacturer must retain treaty documentation and evidence of the shareholder's economic substance for at least 5 years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory rates: 20% withholding on interest and 20% withholding on royalty/licence fees paid to non-residents. Most Egyptian double tax treaties reduce these rates to 10-15%; technical service fees are frequently treated as royalties under Egyptian domestic law and recent ETA practice.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File: aggregate related-party transactions above EGP 10 million per tax year. Master File: group consolidated revenue above EGP 1 billion. Country-by-Country Report: consolidated group revenue of approximately EGP 18 billion (EUR 750 million equivalent). A TP Disclosure Form (Model 40) is mandatory with the Model 200 return whenever controlled transactions are present.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not apply UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations, but the ETA enforces anti-abuse rules under Article 30 of Law No. 91 of 2005, the OECD beneficial ownership test, and substance-over-form principles when granting Investment Law incentives, Free Zone/SEZ rates, or treaty WHT reductions. The EG_LLC must demonstrate physical manufacturing facilities, qualified employees, board decision-making, and genuine EV charger assembly operations in Egypt; a letterbox company cannot retain the 10% SEZ rate or treaty relief.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing Model 200 with inflated COGS, using forged component import invoices, or omitting export letter of credit proceeds from gross revenue.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine of 2 to 5 times the evaded tax plus imprisonment of up to 5 years (Article 133 of Law No. 91 of 2005); automatic reassessment with 2% monthly delay surcharge and asset attachment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Court-ordered joint restitution of evaded tax and penalties, travel ban, disqualification from board service, and imprisonment of the de facto manager.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Interposing a non-resident conduit shareholder or letterbox company without economic substance to claim reduced DTA withholding rates on dividends and royalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA denial of treaty benefits, reclassification of payments as domestically sourced income taxed at 20% withholding, delay surcharges, and administrative fines up to EGP 5 million; commercial blacklisting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable as statutory withholding agents for unpaid WHT, with criminal fines, travel bans, and up to 5 years' imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare or file the Local File, Master File, Country-by-Country Report, or Model 40 TP Disclosure when thresholds are met; pricing controlled party transactions outside the arm's length range.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA TP adjustment to the arm's length profit, 2% monthly surcharge on the additional tax, and fines of EGP 50,000 or more; default profit-rate estimation if documentation is absent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Legal representatives personally liable for non-filing of statutory TP schedules; penalty assessments may be collected from directors' personal assets in cases of gross negligence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Mis-invoicing or double invoicing of DC fast charger exports through affiliated trade companies, or cash structuring of payments to conceal proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law No. 80 of 2002 (amended): fines up to EGP 2 million, confiscation of goods and proceeds, and imprisonment of 5 to 10 years for repeat offenders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Involved officers are personally prosecuted; travel bans, asset freezing, and criminal confiscation ordered by the National Anti-Money Laundering Council.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to e-file the Model 200 return within 4 months of year-end, or failure to remit quarterly Form 205 advance CIT instalments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Late-filing fines of EGP 5,000 to EGP 50,000; 2% monthly late-payment surcharge; automatic ETA assessment and blocking of bank accounts and customs clearance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Travel ban imposed by court order when unpaid corporate tax debt exceeds EGP 100,000; criminal prosecution for flagrant and repeated non-compliance.
